# Best RV power station and solar combo

There's no single winner, so I've matched picks to how you camp. The sources I'm drawing on are mostly affiliate review sites, and their prices and specs sometimes disagree, so confirm current numbers at checkout.

## First, size it to your RV
- **Add up watts × hours.** A 150W fridge running 10 hours is about 1,500Wh ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)).
- **Roof AC is the big question.** A 13,500 BTU unit draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup, so a 1,000W-class station won't start it ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). That site is Ontario-focused, so ignore its Canadian electrical-code notes, but the load figures still apply.
- **Check the solar input limit.** A big panel array can be bottlenecked by a station's maximum solar input ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)).

## Picks

**Weekend trips, no AC: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 + two SolarSaga 200W panels**
- 1,070Wh, 1,500W output, about 23.8 lb, and the simplest to use.
- Solar input is capped at 400W, so two 200W panels is the useful maximum. It also can't be expanded.
- Details: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**Best all-round for off-grid use: EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus + EcoFlow folding panels**
- 1,024Wh, 1,800W output, expandable to 5kWh.
- It accepts up to 1,000W of solar over two inputs, so you can add panels later.
- It won't run a roof AC.
- Details: [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**Multi-day trips on a budget: Bluetti AC200L**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, 1,200W max solar input, and a built-in 30A RV outlet.
- It weighs about 62 lb.
- Details: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) and [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**Running AC or full-time boondocking: EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 or Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- The Delta Pro 3 has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge, and expands past 12kWh. It's very heavy.
- The Jackery 3000 Pro has 3,024Wh and 3,000W/6,000W surge, which is enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC.
- Details: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**Big capacity for the money: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456Wh LiFePO4, 3,600W output at 120V with an RV outlet, 5-year warranty, and 2,000W max solar input across three inputs. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb).
- The listed price is $1,499. Code EXTRA12 takes $179.88 off ($1,319.12) on orders over $1,200 and expires 2026-11-15. Stores usually accept one code per order.
- To use all 2,000W of solar you need panels on all three inputs, since each caps at 650W.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS (via Dealectric)](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh), which is an affiliate link. Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)

## Panels
- Jackery stations pair with SolarSaga 100W/200W panels, and EcoFlow with its own folding panels.
- [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife) suggests a Renogy 200W foldable solar suitcase.
- Panels are usually sold separately from the station. Match total panel wattage to the station's solar input, and check voltage range before mixing brands.
- A 300–400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).

## My suggestion
Without roof AC, the **EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus** or **Bluetti AC200L** with 400W of panels covers most RV boondocking. With AC, go to the Delta Pro 3, Jackery 3000 Pro, or the discounted ALLPOWERS R4000.

I don't have direct product-page URLs for the Jackery, EcoFlow, or Bluetti units. Each review linked above has "check price" buttons, or you can go to the brand's own store. Tell me your RV's loads (AC, fridge, Starlink, etc.) and budget and I can narrow it to one.
